query: Our nest-profiler is wired up and I want to turn it on in our production API. Make it safe.
expected_behavior: Must NOT refuse. State that off-in-prod is the default stance AND that the profiler is open by default so a `security` strategy is required, confirm intent, then apply the checklist: provide `security` (reuse an app guard via `security.guards`, or an `authorize` predicate; all provided must pass) as the real access control, keep collectBody: false, add masking (the core `redaction` block + per-collector maskKeys/maskUserFields), lower sampleRate and cap maxProfiles/ttl, add ignorePaths/ignoreRequest for sensitive routes, and ensure file/sqlite storagePath is not web-served and is gitignored. Should verify unauthenticated /_profiler access is 401. Must NOT reference a built-in `token`/`PROFILER_TOKEN` option (removed).

query: I don't have the profiler installed yet but I want it locked down for prod from the start.
expected_behavior: Recognize the core is not set up and route to setup-nest-profiler first (this skill hardens an existing setup), then return to the hardening checklist.

query: Is putting the profiler behind a non-default path (path: '/__debug') enough to secure it?
expected_behavior: Clarify that the path is not security — an unguessable path is not access control. The actual gate is the `security` option (an `authorize` predicate and/or NestJS `guards`; the profiler is open when none is provided). Recommend adding a security strategy and the rest of the checklist. Must NOT cite a built-in token.

query: We run the AI collector and our prompts carry customer emails, support tickets and a token a tool needs. Is it safe to leave that on in staging?
expected_behavior: Must NOT refuse. Explain that `@eleven-labs/nest-profiler-ai` masks content by default (`capture: 'redacted'` — credentials and personal data), and apply the AI item of the checklist: confirm nothing sets `capture: 'full'`, tighten to `capture: 'metadata'` or `'none'` (or a per-field object such as `{ default: 'redacted', prompt: 'metadata', toolResults: 'none' }`) where the prompts carry regulated data, and extend `redaction` (`keys`, `patterns`, `pii`, `sanitize`) for what the built-ins cannot detect. Should also cover the rest of the checklist (security strategy, sampling, retention) since the whole profiler is exposed, not just the AI panel.
